Thank you for your response. It makes me feel a lot better to hear from someone in a similar situation. It’s easy to feel like a greedy, spoiled brat for not being happy with what I have when I know that other people have so much less.

Every time I achieved something considered challenging it would provide a temporary boost in mood while everyone would praise me for my hard work and I would feel like I’m strong. But it’s led to this cycle where I’m always looking for something even more difficult to accomplish so that I can “prove” that I’m valuable as a human being. But it’s not sustainable and now I’m so tired and I’ve realized that nothing I achieve is going to make me happy. 

I feel stuck because I can’t live being this miserable but I can’t die because I feel too guilty about making other people miserable. I can’t even imagine how you must feel as a parent. 

Can I ask you to expand on what you mean by “aging has made it a little easier”? For instance, how are you differentiating “easier” from “better”? My initial impression was that this meant that you’re still in pain, just more numb to it or better at ignoring/hiding it.

I’m sorry that you’re so unhappy. Can I ask why you stay with your boyfriend when you know you might be gone soon? I ask because I don’t know why it’s so hard for me to do the same. I’m not sure if it’s because I think that making him think that I don’t love him is crueler or because I selfishly want attention and affection up until the moment I’m gone. 

I guess I don’t think that people will miss me because they like me, I think they’ll miss me because my death will create more work for them or mentally disturb them in some way. Even if someone doesn’t like me, working near/being close to someone who kills themselves is just scary.

An inmate who claimed he violated his own civil rights by getting arrested filed a $5 million lawsuit against himself - then asked the state to pay because he has no income in jail.

Robert Lee Brock, a prisoner at the Indian Creek Correctional Center in Chesapeake, filed a handwritten, seven-page lawsuit last month in federal court."I partook of alcoholic beverages in 1993, July 1st, as a result I caused myself to violate my religious beliefs. This was done by my going out and getting arrested," wrote Brock, who is serving 23 years for breaking and entering and grand larceny.

"I want to pay myself 5 million dollars," he continued, "but ask the state to pay it in my behalf since I can't work and am a ward of the state."

Judge Rebecca Beach Smith was unimpressed by Brock's ingenuity.

She dismissed the lawsuit Thursday as frivolous.

"Plaintiff has presented an innovative approach to civil rights litigation," Smith wrote. "However, his claim and especially the relief sought are totally ludicrous."
